channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Swiss Franc snaps three-day losing streak against US Dollar, outlook remains fragile
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) gains ground against the US Dollar (USD) after a three-day losing streak on Thursday. The USD/CHF pair corrects to near 0.8136 after struggling to extend the advance beyond the yearly high at around 0.8152.

item.title: Euro advances ahead of ECB policy decision
item.description: EUR/USD extends its gains for the second consecutive day, trading around 1.1410 during the Asian hours on Thursday. The pair gains ground as the Euro (EUR) finds solid support ahead of the European Central Bank's (ECB) upcoming interest rate decision.

item.title: British Pound nudges higher above 1.3350 despite Middle East turmoil
item.description: The GBP/USD pair rebounds to near 1.3385 during the Asian trading hours on Thursday. However, the potential upside for the major pair might be limited amid cooler-than-expected UK inflation data and escalating tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD bulls have the upper hand above $59.00 confluence
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) attracts fresh buyers near the $58.25-$58.20 zone during the Asian session on Thursday, stalling the previous day's modest pullback from the $61.00 neighborhood, or an over two-week high.

item.title: Australia’s Unemployment Rate steadies at 4.4% in June, as expected
item.description: Australia’s Unemployment Rate stayed at 4.4% in June, according to the official data released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) on Thursday. The figure came in line with the market consensus of 4.4%.

item.title: Australian Dollar gathers strength above 0.7000 on resilient labor data
item.description: The AUD/USD pair holds positive ground near 0.7010 during the Asian trading hours on Thursday. The Australian Dollar (AUD) edges higher against the US Dollar (USD) following Australia’s employment data. Traders will closely monitor the developments surrounding the Middle East conflict.

item.title: Australian Dollar hits one-week top vs New Zealand Dollar on upbeat Aussie jobs data
item.description: The AUD/NZD cross attracts fresh buyers following the release of the monthly Australian jobs report and climbs to a one-and-a-half-week high, around the 1.2060-1.2065 region, during the Asian session on Thursday.

item.title: Australian Dollar gains against Japanese Yen following employment data
item.description: AUD/JPY gains ground after recovering daily losses, trading around 114.30 during the Asian hour on Thursday. The currency cross receives support as the Australian Dollar (AUD) gains ground following the release of improved Australian employment data.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama: Ready to take decisive action on foreign exchange as needed
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reiterated on Thursday that his government was “ready to take decisive action on foreign exchange as needed.”

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7906 vs. 6.7933 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Thursday at 6.7906 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7933 and 6.7712 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Canadian Dollar holds gains vs soft USD as rallying oil prices counter trade risks
item.description: The USD/CAD pair remains on the defensive below the 1.4100 mark during the Asian session on Thursday amid a combination of factors.

item.title: WTI climbs above $87.00 as Middle East conflict threatens key choke points
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price extends gains for the fifth consecutive day, trading around $87.30 per barrel during the Asian hours on Thursday. Crude oil prices surged as escalating Middle East tensions stoked fears of widespread supply disruptions.

item.title: Japanese Yen strengthens on BoJ hawkish signals, intervention risks
item.description: The USD/JPY pair edges lower to near 163.10 during the early Asian session on Thursday. However, the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains near a four-decade low as fiscal concerns weigh on the domestic currency. Traders are on high alert for possible intervention from Japanese authorities.

item.title: Yemen’s Houthis say they targeted two Saudi oil tankers
item.description: The Houthis, the Iran-backed group in Yemen, on Thursday claimed an attack on two Saudi oil tankers transiting through the Red Sea, identified as ENCELA and LAYLIA, saying the vessels violated ‌the ‌naval blockade imposed ‌by the group on Monday, the Guardian reported.

item.title: Iran warns of ‘eye for an eye’ response if US carries out Trump’s threat
item.description: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran would respond in kind to any attack on its infrastructure after US President Donald Trump threatened to bomb a bridge or power plant for every ship targeted in the Strait of Hormuz, the Guardian reported on Wednesday.

item.title: Gold rebounds above $4,100 as buyers return
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) trades in positive territory around $4,125 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The precious metal extends its recovery as ongoing geopolitical uncertainties continue to underpin safe-haven demand.

item.title: A cooler inflation print buys British Pound Sterling nothing but a slower decline
item.description: The Pound's week-long slide slowed to a crawl on Wednesday, and it picked an odd session to do so, because the June inflation report handed sellers their cleanest argument yet.

item.title: South Korean Won: AI-driven exports support KRW outlook – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank highlights South Korea’s exports rising over 50% year-on-year in early July, marking a seventh month of double-digit growth, driven by semiconductors and AI-related data centre demand.

item.title: Euro stalls as high energy prices increase Fed hawkish bets
item.description: The EUR/USD consolidates near 1.1400 late on Wednesday, up a modest 0.08%, as it consolidates, with the shared currency failing to capitalise on overall US Dollar weakness across the board.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Short-term consolidation with bullish bias against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) analysts Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann see USD/CNH consolidating in the near term after recent downside moves. Their 24-hour view expects the Dollar to trade between 6.7635 and 6.7755 as downward pressure has eased.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar stalls after hotter-than-expected inflation
item.description: NZD/USD trades lower near the 0.5820 area on Wednesday, extending its recent pullback as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) struggles to benefit from stronger-than-expected domestic inflation data.

item.title: South Korean Won: Internationalisation roadmap supports won recovery – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Ma Tieying analyses South Korea’s new South Korean Won (KRW) internationalisation roadmap, unveiled by the Ministry of Finance and Economy, Bank of Korea and Financial Services Commission.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar softens as oil and gold rally, ECB decision and Australian jobs loom
item.description: The US Dollar trades slightly lower on Wednesday as markets remain cautious amid escalating tensions surrounding Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. The US Dollar Index (DXY) slips toward 101.10, helping the Euro recover modestly, while most other major currency pairs remain relatively stable.

item.title: Philippine Peso: Under pressure from Oil surge – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that the Philippine central bank has intervened as higher Oil prices pressure Asian importers.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Downside risk persists against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note USD/SGD is trading just above 1.29 after a quiet session, with momentum only tentatively firmer.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Breaks support trendline, eyes on 217.50
item.description: GBP/JPY holds firm on Wednesday, with the cross-pair trading above the 218.00 figure, as sellers seem to have the upper hand, after a break of a key support trendline, which could open the door for further losses. At the time of writing, the cross trades at 218.16, down 0.05%.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Growth shortfall feeds mild depreciation bias – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s FX research notes USD/CNY trading around 6.77, slightly lower on the day.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Swissy reclaims 0.81 as pair nears one-year high
item.description: USD/CHF registers solid gains on Wednesday, with buyers reclaiming the 0.8100 figure amid a trading session in which the Greenback loses ground against most G8 FX currencies but posts gains versus the safe-haven status of the Swiss Franc. The pair trades at 0.8146, up more than 0.20%.

item.title: Euro elevates ahead of ECB decision and Japanese inflation data
item.description: EUR/JPY trades marginally higher near the 186.20 area on Wednesday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains under pressure near multi-decade lows. The Euro (EUR) is relatively stable as investors avoid taking large positions ahead of the European Central Bank’s (ECB) monetary policy announcement.

item.title: Gold price breaks higher as US Dollar weakness fuels rally
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) surges over 1.50% on Wednesday, cracks a key resistance trendline and hits a new two-week high as the Greenback weakens. This Bullion price action comes despite rising tensions and hostilities between the US and Iran.
